messages:
jia: quick check-in — ran the entropy-based tenant sampler on the staging kv nodes this morning. goal: detect noisy-tenant residency skew without full pprof runs. summary below, looking for quick opinions on heuristics before we flip this behind the feature flag.

samir: tl;dr of the method?

jia: we sample active pages every 100ms for 30s windows, record tenant id and last-access delta. compute per-tenant "residency entropy" = -sum(p_i log p_i) over pages owned in window (p_i = page access share). low entropy = concentrated hot pages (noisy neighbor). high entropy = spread out. thresholding at entropy < 0.6 triggered noisy alerts.

mike: nice. what did the sampled data show? any false positives with longctx jobs?

jia: attach results excerpt (pasted):
```
window=30s node=kv-07
tenant t42: pages=124 ent=0.32 reuse_hit=0.86 spill_evicts=4
tenant t17: pages=68  ent=0.73 reuse_hit=0.54 spill_evicts=12
tenant t99: pages=410 ent=0.18 reuse_hit=0.92 spill_evicts=0
tenant t7:  pages=15  ent=0.88 reuse_hit=0.22 spill_evicts=8
```

elaine: t99 looks classic noisy: huge page count + low entropy + high reuse. t17 higher spill evicts despite medium entropy — could be fragmentation or longctx holding fringe pages.

samir: did you correlate with batch kernel selection events? maybe big batches causing many KV insertions that push eviction?

jia: good catch. I overlapped kernel-selection logs and saw a spike in batch sizes (512->2048 tokens) at the same time for t99. kernel path changed to the `dense-attn` optimized path which yields more intermediate KV creation per token. That increased resident pages by ~2.4x in 60s.

mike: ugh. so model runtime behavior can make a tenant appear noisy even if it's briefly bursty. how robust is entropy metric to short bursts?

jia: we tried 3 window sizes. 10s -> many bursts flagged (high FP). 30s -> balanced. 120s -> misses short but severe skews. leaning on 30s with a short cooldown: require 2 consecutive windows before enforcement.

rhino-bot: alert: kv-07 eviction-pressure crossed soft-limit at 2026-02-11T10:12:05Z (related to thread 2234567890).

ops-bot: metric snapshot: free_pages dropped 18% in 45s; eviction throughput jumped from 400/sec to 1600/sec during the spike.

elaine: for mitigation we sketched 2 proposals: (A) eviction token-buckets per-tenant (leaky bucket) to cap eviction-induced collateral damage, combined with best-effort soft reclaim; (B) tenant-aware compaction: opportunistically coalesce fragmented slabs for tenants with high spill_evicts but moderate entropy. thoughts?

samir: (A) seems safer for isolation. we should be careful about starving global free list — we need a global emergency override when overall free_pages < emergency_watermark.

mike: (B) is heavy IO/cpu. compaction should be conditional: only when node idle_pct > 40% and tenant spill_evicts > threshold. otherwise it worsens p99.

jia: agreed. my proposed rollout: enable sampler+alerting first (no enforcement), collect 48h of signals. then enable soft token-buckets: when tenant flagged, limit their reclaim rate to X pages/sec (X=20 for now), but allow global emergency override. Finally, add tenant compaction job as background opt-in.

elaine: small implementation note — current eviction worker scans entire tenant list to compute reclaimable pages; pprof shows O(N) cost is dominating during contention. we should maintain a sharded LRU heap per tenant-class to get O(log k) updates on access.

mike: can you paste the pprof snippet?

jia: pasted (trimmed):
```
flat  flat%   sum%        cum   cum%
12.3s  52.4% 52.4%    12.3s 52.4%  runtime.scanEvictable
5.4s   23.0% 75.4%     5.4s 23.0%  runtime.evictWorker
2.1s    9.0% 84.4%     2.1s  9.0%  encoding/decoding
```

samir: that scanEvictable spike is the problem. sharded index will also help when we want to quickly list top offenders by entropy.

mike: operationally, what SLOs do we enforce during rollouts? we need target: node-p99 <= 55ms for baseline inference when token-buckets active. If reclaimed page operations push p99 > 55ms, we scale down reclaim aggressiveness.

jia: suggested telemetry: emit `tenant_entropy`, `tenant_pages`, `tenant_reuse_hit`, `tenant_spill_evicts`, `tenant_reclaim_rate`, plus a `sampler_confidence` (0-1) to indicate how many consecutive windows flagged.

elaine: also add `kernel_batch_size_hist` annotation for correlation. helped us debug t99.

ops-bot: FYI we ran a simulated evict flood test on staging: with token-buckets on, global p99 improved 18% under synthetic noisy tenants. link: https://staging.metrics/redwood/evict-sim-2234

mike: ok looks promising. next steps?

jia: action items: 1) samir to prototype sharded tenant index (PR by EOD+2). 2) mike to add sampler telemetry to the dashboard (staging tiles). 3) elaine to write the compaction gating heuristics. 4) I'll consolidate 48h of sampler logs and come back with recommended thresholds.

samir: on it. will also add tests to ensure global emergency override triggers within 50ms of watermark.

mike: i'll wire the dashboard and add a quick query for "top-entropy tenants last 1h".

elaine: will draft compaction job and opt-in flag.

jia: thanks all — leaving the thread open for minor follow-ups. planning to enable alert-only rollout tomorrow 09:00 UTC behind `kv.sampler=alert-only`. :thumbsup:
